- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.25) or volatile, model often underestimates or overshoots early; adjust downward by 3–8% for first 5–7 days of forecast horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast decline to 3–5% below peak unless sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “0.25” (neutral/low), model tends to drift upward; apply downward bias of 1–4% for 3–5 days ahead.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates mid-term (days 10–25) due to momentum bias; reduce mid-range values by 2–5% if sentiment is flat or negative.
